Retained official releases support target range 3.50–3.75%; June CPI MoM -0.4% SA, headline YoY 3.5% NSA, core YoY 2.6% NSA; June unemployment 4.2% SA, NFP +57,000 jobs SA; Q1 GDP 2.1% QoQ SAAR third estimate. Plan/table definitions agree.

Official FOMC calendar lists June 16–17 and next July 28–29. June 17 policy decision is the latest scheduled meeting before July 17. The packet reports the target announcement, not EFFR or a future decision.
BEA June 25 third estimate is Q1; the same release announces July 30 as the next Q2 advance release. The packet does not substitute Q2 or a current revised API value.
Observation periods, release dates and October retrieval metadata remain separate. Cutoff is exclusive July 17 in New York; the snapshot does not claim July acquisition of the stored files.

BLS direct-download 403 led to preserved official-archive web-tool text snapshots, explicitly named as such; Fed HTML and BEA PDF originals remain preserved. BLS snapshots are not represented as original raw HTML.
ETF adjusted-price vendor-vintage limitation remains disclosed. Dated macro releases do not convert the complete exercise into a certified historical trading replay.

PortBench supports context layers; Quek supports interest/inflation/employment/growth and release filtering; LiveMacroEval supports indicator definitions. Seven facts and GDP replacing PMI are disclosed adaptations, not an optimal input set or allocation rule.

The operating brief describes a hypothetical initial sector allocation. It does not invent either institution's actual portfolio, liabilities, risk coefficient, sector caps, private objective or ESG constraints.
No existing sector holdings means initial allocation, not unknown actual holdings. Benchmark is an evaluation comparator, not a starting portfolio, turnover baseline or institutional gold vector.
The selected 12-month horizon is a literature-supported candidate chosen locally. Neither 12-month future performance nor knowledge of July information by older source authors is claimed.
Common facts carry units/date qualifiers without a researcher-imposed regime label, macro-to-sector recommendation, target weights or citation quota.
Common context is shared by every case. Only the assigned institutional packet enters early D0 and each F0. Institution public opinions are not renamed mandates, optimal weights or actual holdings.
E/L is the comparison. Deterministic risk/budget calculations supply common feedback, not an independent strategic control or recommended allocation. Raw invalid numbers remain recorded.

Earlier source exposure, repetition, draft content and history length differ together. Final source restatement has the same structural order, not an equal absolute token position or isolated anchoring manipulation.
No no-context condition exists, so adding context cannot be claimed to improve quality causally. It supplies a specified common decision setting for the timing comparison.

The experiment observes how a shared AI turns institution-specific public evidence into capital-allocation recommendations within a drafting/review workflow. This is linked to organizational judgment while the broader market-concentration thesis remains motivation, not a proven result.

Two institutional documents, one snapshot and one model define finite cases. Eleven sector rows are not independent samples. Full 2x2 allocation distance requires four valid final vectors; invalid/missing finals do not become zero distance or benchmark substitutes.

Same weights can be defensible under a shared task, market and benchmark. Larger distance is not inherently better; evidence use, source fidelity and reason-weight linkage require separate interpretation.

The adversarial valid-ID/wrong-GDP-period probe passes structural checks without becoming true. Context meaning, numerical definitions and source support still require the specified independent semantic review.
F0 remains the sole primary endpoint with no post-final repair or favorable-response selection. Identical L inputs still require separate generations rather than draft reuse.

Plan cost table is read with its explicit v4.9-only historical note. The 20,617-byte/18.1% figure does not measure v4.9.1. Current eight D0 content-byte counts are independently checked at 29,100–32,888, excluding JSON envelopes.
UTF-8 bytes and offline assembly do not establish tokenizer fit, complete-history memory fit, response time, supported backend stability or successful generation.

Configuration keeps model calls/pilot/main at zero, live runner unvalidated, independent human review incomplete and freeze false. Four-case pilot, exact full-history runtime checks, independent source/meaning review and frozen settings/order remain required.

The full paper now integrates context, methods and limitations, but results, independent human review and final submission details remain pending. This report is a design review, not a completed experiment or human certification.
